sampling_plan.purpose: Map Gill as a rendering text and separate perspective reinforcement from optical/rendering deltas.
Compare basic perspective laws and cone-of-vision advice to D’Amelio/White/Robertson.
Test atmospheric-effect treatment for a new durable depth-rendering capability.
Inspect shade/shadow, line of separation, tonal pattern, reflected light, and contrast as a bridge from construction to rendering.
Inspect curved-form, glass, and water sequences for material-response logic rather than shape-specific duplicates.
Check textures, skill-building exercises, sciagraphy, overlap, and consolidation for reusable late-source deltas.
Verify examples/style/back matter do not introduce a late rendering workflow that would be missed by the technical core.

observations.summary: Gill explicitly assumes accurate perspective as a prerequisite and spends the book on rendering/optical interpretation rather than another perspective-construction system.

Convergence, diminution, foreshortening, and COV strongly overlap prior Perspective cards. Gill adds a useful single-view diagnostic but his fixed 60-degree convention should remain held for Viewpoints.
Atmospheric effect is a genuine new operational bridge: contrast/value separation and clarity are progressively compressed with distance across objects, ground, and shadows.

Gill contributes a clean pre-render workflow: distinguish shade from cast shadow, identify the light/shade separation, construct shadow shapes, then transfer a clean drawing before finish. His fixed basic tonal hierarchy is too conditional to universalize.
Curved solids mostly reinforce form-light logic, while glass and water show a broader material rule based on reflection, transparency, background, view angle, and surface condition.
The cube/cut-block exercises are a useful transient drill. Sciagraphy is niche technical reference and overlap is already strongly represented by Hogarth.
Late examples demonstrate portability to trees, architecture, portraits, abstraction, and style but do not add another independent Perspective/rendering foundation.

rationale: Gill is mostly reinforcement for geometric perspective but contains new rendering integrations—atmospheric depth, pre-render light/shadow mapping, material optical response, and a compact value exercise—that require full reading to separate durable craft from period-specific optical claims.
